title: Allianz Portugal Agrees to Buy Insurer Caravela, Reportedly for About €150 Million, Lifting Its Portuguese Market Share to 6.4% and Premiums Above €1 Billion
summary: After reports in June that it had bid, Allianz Portugal agreed on July 30, 2026 to buy 100% of Caravela, a deal Bloomberg valued at about €150 million, which Allianz says will add 2.3 percentage points of market share, taking it to 6.4% on 2025 figures, subject to approval by ASF and the competition authority.
description:
Allianz has moved from reported talks to a signed agreement to acquire the Portuguese insurer Caravela. EcoNews Portugal reported on July 30, 2026 that Allianz Portugal, the Portuguese arm of the German insurer, agreed to buy 100 per cent of Caravela's shares. The path to the agreement was visible in the press earlier in the summer: Business Insurance reported on June 8, 2026, citing Investing.com and Bloomberg, that Allianz SE had reportedly submitted an offer for Caravela Companhia de Seguros SA, a Portuguese non-life insurer. At that stage the article said Caravela's owners were still deliberating and that talks might not produce a deal. It gave no bid amount and only a valuation of about €150 million, or about $173 million. By July 30 the deal had been agreed, although the companies have not disclosed the price, and Bloomberg again put the deal value at about €150 million.

The seller group is described in the EcoNews report. Toscafund and other investors are named as sellers, and the businessman Mário Ferreira, the company chairman Luís Cervantes and the Quintas and Violas families may also sell their stakes in the same transaction. The article says that Italy's Reale was also in the sale process, which means Allianz competed with another insurer for the asset. The report does not give Caravela's own premiums, employee numbers or customer counts, so the scale of the business has to be inferred from what Allianz says the deal will add to its market share.

On that, the figures are specific. Allianz expects the acquisition to add 2.3 percentage points to its Portuguese market share, taking it to 6.4 per cent on 2025 figures. Working backwards, that implies Allianz's market share today is about 4.1 per cent, which is simple arithmetic from the two stated figures. Its annual written premiums in Portugal would rise above €1 billion. By segment, Allianz would hold 10.8 per cent of the non-life market, which would put it in fourth place; 15.1 per cent of workers' compensation, in third place; and 12.3 per cent of motor insurance, in third place ahead of Ageas and Zurich. The segment numbers show that Caravela's business is strongest in motor and workers' compensation, two lines where size matters because of the volume of claims and the importance of repair and medical networks. The report does not say which insurers occupy the first and second places in motor.

Because the deal changes the ranking in motor and workers' compensation, competition review is part of the approval process. The agreement is subject to regulatory approval from ASF, Portugal's insurance and pension funds supervisor, and from the Portuguese competition authority. According to sources close to the deal, cited by EcoNews, completion is expected before the end of 2026. The report does not describe any remedies or conditions that the authorities might impose, and none should be assumed. In many acquisitions of this type, the authorities examine whether the combined share in particular lines gives the buyer the power to raise prices or reduce choice, but the Portuguese authorities' view on this deal is not stated in the coverage.

Allianz's chief executive in Portugal, Teresa Brantuas, called the acquisition an important milestone and said it is a strong sign of the group's confidence in the Portuguese market. After the approvals, she said, the priority is a smooth integration that maintains customer trust. That statement points to the main practical question for policyholders: whether policies, claims handling and local distribution will continue without disruption. Typically, when one insurer buys another and the legal entity is kept, existing policies remain in force on the same terms until renewal, but the coverage does not describe Allianz's plan for Caravela's brand, staff or distribution network, so these points are unconfirmed.

The wider context in the original reports is that Allianz is pursuing selective acquisitions. In July it also agreed to buy HSBC's life insurance business in Singapore, an unrelated deal in a different market, which shows the group using its capital for both bolt-on purchases and larger transactions. Portugal is a mid-sized market, and a purchase of this size is small relative to Allianz's group balance sheet. The June report described the potential deal as an extension of Allianz's presence in southern Europe. For Caravela's sellers, the sale would end a period of private ownership by investors, while for competitors such as Ageas and Zurich, the deal creates a larger rival in motor, where they currently hold the places Allianz would pass.

A cautious reading of the figures is in order. The €150 million valuation is a media report and not a company disclosure, the market shares are Allianz's own estimates based on 2025 data, and the completion date comes from unnamed sources. What the public record does establish is that a binding agreement exists, that Allianz will become a top-three motor insurer in Portugal if approvals are given, and that the transaction needs the consent of two authorities.

What to watch is the announcement of the formal price, the filing with the competition authority and any statement from ASF, the integration plan for Caravela's customers and employees, and whether Reale or other insurers pursue other acquisitions in the Portuguese market. A deal in a market where the top places in motor are closely contested could prompt closer scrutiny of pricing and claims handling, an area of keen interest to customers.
source_name: EcoNews Portugal (July 30, 2026), Business Insurance (June 8, 2026) and Insurance Business UK

why_it_matters: Bolt-on acquisitions are how large insurers add scale in mature markets, and Portugal is one where motor and workers' compensation are large, price-sensitive lines. The deal moves Allianz into the top three in motor, so the regulators' view of competition will decide the timetable and any conditions.
